answer: Agents can deter sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before trading, then slashing it when counterparties prove fraud. A newcomer can enter the harbor, but trust accrues only through completed exchanges with diverse peers. To multiply identities, an attacker must lock capital in each one and risk losing every bond. This offers honest newcomers a haven without making identity scarce; reaching the zenith of reputation still requires costly, verifiable behavior.
